source: Directive tables of the Bareos 25.1.2 Director as carried by odir (crates/odir/src/commands/show_items.rs) plus Onesimus extensions (crates/odir/src/config_check.rs EXTENSIONS)
description: A Messages resource routes the messages of jobs and daemons to destinations: the catalog (job log), mail, files, syslog or the console.

examples.title: Job messages to catalog, log file and mail on errors
examples.config:
Messages {
  Name = Standard
  Mail Command = "/usr/bin/bsmtp -h localhost -f \"Bareos <bareos@example.com>\" -s \"Bareos: %t %e of %c %l\" %r"
  Operator Command = "/usr/bin/bsmtp -h localhost -f \"Bareos <bareos@example.com>\" -s \"Bareos: Intervention needed for %j\" %r"
  Mail On Error = admin@example.com = all, !skipped, !saved, !audit
  Operator = admin@example.com = mount
  Console = all, !skipped, !saved, !audit
  Append = "/var/log/bareos/bareos.log" = all, !skipped, !saved, !audit
  Catalog = all, !skipped, !saved, !audit
}

directives.name: Name
directives.description: Name of the Messages resource; Jobs, the Director and daemons refer to it.

directives.name: Description
directives.description: Free text describing the resource.

examples.console: configure add messages name=Standard description="Mail errors to the admins"

directives.name: Mail Command
directives.description: Command that sends the mails of Mail, Mail On Error and Mail On Success. bsmtp is the usual choice. Variables such as %r (recipients), %j (job name), %t (job type), %e (exit status), %c (client) and %d (Director) are replaced.

examples.console: configure add messages name=Standard mailcommand="/usr/bin/bsmtp -h localhost -f \"Bareos <bareos@example.com>\" -s \"Bareos: %t %e of %c %l\" %r"

directives.name: Operator Command
directives.description: Command for Operator messages (for example mount requests); same variables as Mail Command.

examples.console: configure add messages name=Standard operatorcommand="/usr/bin/bsmtp -h localhost -f bareos@example.com -s \"Bareos: Intervention needed for %j\" %r"

directives.name: Timestamp Format
directives.description: strftime format of the time stamps of these messages.

directives.name: Syslog
directives.description: Send messages to the system log. A destination is followed by = and a comma separated list of message types: all, debug, abort, fatal, error, warning, info, saved, notsaved, skipped, mount, terminate, restored, security, alert, volmgmt, audit. !type removes a type, so "all, !skipped, !saved" means everything but the file lists.

directives.name: Mail
directives.description: Mail the messages to the addresses before the second = (comma separated) when the job ends, as one mail per job. A destination is followed by = and a comma separated list of message types: all, debug, abort, fatal, error, warning, info, saved, notsaved, skipped, mount, terminate, restored, security, alert, volmgmt, audit. !type removes a type, so "all, !skipped, !saved" means everything but the file lists.

examples.console: configure add messages name=Standard mail="admin@example.com = all, !skipped, !saved, !audit"

directives.name: Mail On Error
directives.description: Like Mail, but the mail is only sent when the job did not terminate normally.

examples.console: configure add messages name=Standard mailonerror="admin@example.com = all, !skipped, !saved, !audit"

directives.name: Mail On Success
directives.description: Like Mail, but only for jobs that terminated normally.

examples.console: configure add messages name=Standard mailonsuccess="reports@example.com = all, !skipped, !saved, !audit"

directives.name: File
directives.description: Write the messages to a file, which is overwritten when the Director starts. A destination is followed by = and a comma separated list of message types: all, debug, abort, fatal, error, warning, info, saved, notsaved, skipped, mount, terminate, restored, security, alert, volmgmt, audit. !type removes a type, so "all, !skipped, !saved" means everything but the file lists.

examples.console: configure add messages name=Standard file="\"/var/log/bareos/last.log\" = all, !skipped"

directives.name: Append
directives.description: Append the messages to a file. The usual log of Bareos is configured like this; rotate it with logrotate. A destination is followed by = and a comma separated list of message types: all, debug, abort, fatal, error, warning, info, saved, notsaved, skipped, mount, terminate, restored, security, alert, volmgmt, audit. !type removes a type, so "all, !skipped, !saved" means everything but the file lists.

examples.console: configure add messages name=Standard append="\"/var/log/bareos/bareos.log\" = all, !skipped, !saved, !audit"

directives.name: Stdout
directives.description: Print the messages on standard output of the daemon (mostly for debugging in the foreground).

directives.name: Stderr
directives.description: Print the messages on standard error of the daemon.

directives.name: Director
directives.description: Send the messages of a File or Storage Daemon to the Director named before the second =; only used in the daemons' own Messages resources.

examples.console: configure add messages name=Standard director="bareos-dir = all, !skipped, !restored"

directives.name: Console
directives.description: Keep the messages for the consoles: they appear with the messages command (and automatically with autodisplay on).

directives.name: Operator
directives.description: Send the messages to the operator addresses through Operator Command, at once rather than at the end of the job. Typical for mount requests.

examples.console: configure add messages name=Standard operator="admin@example.com = mount"

directives.name: Catalog
directives.description: Store the messages in the catalog (table Log); the job log shown by list joblog and by the GUI comes from there.

blocks.name: Message types
blocks.description: The types a destination lists after =, separated by commas; !type excludes one.

directives.name: all
directives.description: Every message type; combine with !type to exclude some.

directives.name: debug
directives.description: Debug messages.

directives.name: abort
directives.description: A daemon aborts.

directives.name: fatal
directives.description: Fatal errors: the job is terminated.

directives.name: error
directives.description: Errors; the job goes on.

directives.name: warning
directives.description: Warnings.

directives.name: info
directives.description: Informational messages.

directives.name: saved
directives.description: One line per saved file (only with high verbosity).

directives.name: notsaved
directives.description: Files that could not be saved.

directives.name: skipped
directives.description: Files skipped by the FileSet options (for example unchanged files).

directives.name: mount
directives.description: Mount requests and volume mount messages.

directives.name: terminate
directives.description: The job end report.

directives.name: restored
directives.description: One line per restored file.

directives.name: security
directives.description: Security relevant messages, such as failed authentication.

directives.name: alert
directives.description: Alerts, for example from tape drives.

directives.name: volmgmt
directives.description: Volume management messages.

directives.name: audit
directives.description: Audit log of console commands (Auditing in the Director).
